text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Central bank releases 800 million naira in commercial banks' stabilisation securities as part of its efforts to boost their liquidity.

- Canada is progressively shutting down its diplomatic mission in Lagos following the closure of Nigeria's mission in Ottawa last month. Daily Times gathers that the mission has now shut its doors to the media.
- Big commercial banks have begun to shun deposits from the Petroleum Trust Fund because of their inability to find borrowers even at low interest rates.
- Stock exchange official says the strategy of foreign investors has moved from outright capital flight to sectoral transfer of investments within Nigeria.

- A central bank official at the weekend revealed that a report published mistakenly by the bank last week showing a budget deficit had ignored 31 billion naira in government receipts from foreign exchange transactions.
- Nigerian Breweries says it secured the bottling franchise for Schweppes soft drinks without any financial commitment.
- Oil minister redeploys officials of the Pipelines and Products Marketing Company at the Warri oil refinery.
- Government has set up an administrative panel to probe an alleged 1.115 billion naira fraud at the Federal Environmental Protection Agency at its Port Harcourt zone.
